session.name: MPI-607 session 26 - Flow B's graph proven, then Fabio's own testing put the whole VC design in doubt

goal.original: Start the TEXT-TO-SPEECH flow (Flow B) via /mpi-add-flow.
goal.summary: NO CARD WAS CREATED - MPI-607 already owns Flow B and was already in `doing`. The graph shape was built and proven (4/4 routes, 4/4 distinct outputs) and four real defects were measured and recorded. THEN Fabio's own bench testing reached a verdict that outranks all of it: VC is too inconsistent, it destroys voices, and what has been built does not resemble a product. NOTHING WAS WIRED INTO THE APP - no op, no FlowDef, no registry edit - which is fortunate, because the design may not survive. The next session installs DramaBox on his bench to see whether DramaBox + Chatterbox can be combined into something shippable.

completed: BOARD CHECKED FIRST, AND NO CARD WAS NEEDED. MPI-607 'TTS in Vision' was already in `doing` and its checklist already carried `Gate 2 FLOW B`. Its files.json already covers flowsRegistry / commandRegistry / operationRegistry / operation_registry.json / comfy_workflows. Every file claim on flowsRegistry.js is STALE (Aug 22-23, 120min timeout), so nothing was blocked.

FLOW B'S GRAPH SHAPE PROVEN ON THE BENCH, 4/4 quadrants, `research/flow_b_graph_probe.py`. Two independent axes fanned out in the GRAPH as MpiAnySwitch banks off two MpiInts - zero app code. THE CHECK THAT MATTERED was not that four runs produced audio but that all four outputs are DISTINCT (4/4 sha256, envelope r 0.07-0.48): a lost switch selector does not error, it silently pins every run to any_1 and still succeeds.

THREE GRAPH FACTS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: MpiAnySwitch is LAZY (a straight read runs with an EMPTY perf-clip loader and `block_if_empty` armed, and it never fires); the switch's `*` output links into typed AUDIO and FLOAT inputs; and `language` is a COMBO that REFUSES a link (`received_type(STRING) mismatch input_type([...23])`), so a language literal must be BAKED one arm per shipped language.

THE MULTILINGUAL TRAILING-NOISE DEFECT IS SOLVED: `repetition_penalty` 2.0, the node's own default, is the cause. 24 warm runs, 6 seeds x 4 configs: 3/6 overshoot at 2.0 (4.97 / 11.18 / 11.97s against a 3.90s base), two with tails 2.65x and 3.05x flatter than their own body and ~0 voiced frames = hiss. 0/12 failures at 1.5 or 1.2. SHIP 1.5. Both of Fabio's symptoms are one event - warm, the model costs ~1s over base and is slow only on the runs where it never stops.

CHAIN ORDER SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT: order A (TTS(perf clip) -> VC(voice)) wins. Cosine 0.897 vs the picked voice against a 0.811 neutral-TTS calibration, f0 within 1.20 st. Order B (Fabio's proposed identity-first order) held cosine (0.827) and failed on pitch: +5.35 st, 135 -> 184 Hz, out of R2 into R3. Only the f0 column sees it - CAMPPlus x-vectors are pitch-invariant by construction. His ear agreed with the numbers unprompted.

THE AXIS IS LANGUAGE, NOT ACCENT - and this REVERSED a recommendation I had already written down. Accent-on-English does not dependably work (measured, five clips, his ear). But Fabio's own testing showed Portuguese text through the BASE model is unusable while multilingual-with-Portuguese gives real Brazilian Portuguese. So multilingual SHIPS, for any language that is not English, and everything I proposed dropping with it is load-bearing again. The lesson is recorded in validation.md: a negative result is only as good as the question it answered, and 'accent on English does not work' very nearly deleted a model the product needs for an unrelated reason.

A LABEL THAT LIES, caught by Fabio: the node's dropdown says `Portuguese (pt)` and delivers BRAZILIAN Portuguese. Recorded as an obligation on the whole shipped list, not a Portuguese footnote - the list is bare ISO 639-1 codes which carry no variant at all, so Spanish, Chinese, Norwegian and the default English are unverified on identical grounds. Same rule MPI-622 set for `accent`: a wrong label is worse than a missing one.

TWO STALE CLAIMS FIXED in `docs/playbooks/add-flow/existing-flows/voice-changer.md` that would have misled this build: the performance clips it said do not exist have shipped (30 of them), and the accent-survival question it listed as gating Flow B is closed. Also corrected the size: the five TTS dep ids are 3.19 GB; the often-quoted 4.25 GB is all SEVEN weights, i.e. the character route.

BENCH LEFT SET UP FOR FABIO'S OWN TESTING: both candidate graphs as loadable workflows (`G:/ComfyUi/ComfyUI/user/default/workflows/MPI607_FlowB_OrderA.json` and `_OrderB.json`), and the entire shipped library staged as wav - `input/mpi607_voices/<REGISTER>_<id>.wav` (56) and `input/mpi607_perf/<REGISTER>_<emotion>.wav` (30), register-prefixed so pairing a voice to its grid needs no manifest lookup. Index at `input/mpi607_index.json`.

Four commits: 4a81ee62 (graph shape + rp defect), 0a6feec1 (chain order + accent), 8290ebf4 (the LANGUAGE correction + emotion sweep), 8e929158 (the variant-label rule). Board validated clean before the peer's MPI-629 appeared.
pending: INSTALL DRAMABOX ON THE BENCH - THIS IS THE NEXT JOB AND IT COMES BEFORE ANY MORE FLOW B WIRING. Weights go in `G:/CubricModels`, which IS the bench's `extra_model_paths.yaml` `base_path` (verified). Fabio's reason, and it outranks everything measured this session: *'What I've been testing does not resemble something that could be a product. There are too many inconsistencies, especially with performance. VC is very inconsistent. It destroys voices ... it just changes the voices too much.'* He wants to see whether DramaBox + Chatterbox combine into a good product.

VRAM IS NOT A GATE - THAT CONCERN WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN (Fabio, 2026-08-27). The '24GB VRAM' in this card's rejection table was what the AUTHOR happened to run on (an H100), never a stated requirement, and it was carried into the handoff as though it were one. ComfyUI OFFLOADS: models with 40GB transformers have already been run on this very machine. DramaBox's files are ~6GB. His instruction is explicit: *'just because the user used an H100 doesn't mean that it doesn't work on smaller cards. I want to test it.'* INSTALL IT AND TEST IT - do not re-derive a VRAM objection, and do not let a spec sheet end the evaluation before a generation has been attempted.

ONE CHECK THAT IS STILL WORTH DOING FIRST, because it is cheap and it fails SILENTLY: does DramaBox's node pack resolve weights through `folder_paths`? `ComfyUI_Fill-ChatterBox` computes its model dir from `__file__` and NEVER reads `extra_model_paths.yaml`, which is exactly why the chatterbox weights had to ship as `targetPath` deps. If DramaBox does the same, weights placed in `G:/CubricModels` are invisible to it and it will `hf_hub_download` its own copy instead - no error, just a surprise download and a duplicated 6GB. This is a grep of the pack, not a gate on whether to proceed.

A THIRD ROUTE TO THE SAME USE CASE, raised by Fabio and not previously on this card: **LTX 2.3 already ships in Vision, it TAKES AUDIO AS A REFERENCE, and it emits video WITH audio.** LTX 2.5 lands with a coming ComfyUI bump. They are video models and they are slow, but for a performance-carrying spoken line that may not disqualify them. Worth evaluating alongside DramaBox rather than after it - the whole reason DramaBox is being re-opened is that Chatterbox VC destroys voices, and a model that takes a reference performance natively is attacking the same problem from a different side.

DRAMABOX WAS REJECTED ONCE, ON THE RECORD - re-opening it is Fabio's explicit call, but carry the reasons so they get re-checked rather than rediscovered: LTX-2 Community licence, 240 HF downloads/30d, stale since 2026-05-23, 24GB VRAM, no weight sharing. `plan.md` model-verdicts table.

DO NOT WIRE THE OP OR THE FlowDef YET. The graph shape is proven but the DESIGN it implements is what Fabio has called into question. Wiring 4 registry files against a design that may be replaced is exactly the work to not do. Nothing has been touched in the app - keep it that way until the DramaBox verdict is in.

EMOTION DOES NOT APPEAR TO CARRY THROUGH THE MULTILINGUAL MODEL. Four cells swept on the real product path (Portuguese, order A): all land at or BELOW the neutral read (104.8-121.7 Hz against a 121.7 Hz neutral and a 167.3 Hz angry reference) where an angry read must sit above. No cell rescues it. EAR CHECK OWED - clips in `%LOCALAPPDATA%/cubric-vision/mpi607/mtl_emotion/`. If it holds, non-English gets no performed reads and that is a product decision, not a bug.

STILL NEEDS FABIO, neither blocked on the bench: WHICH LANGUAGES SHIP (each needs its variant confirmed by ear before it is labelled), and WHETHER THE 3.2 GB multilingual set is bundled or an optional install (`requiredDeps` cannot express optional - his own parked question).

THE 18 R2/R4/R5 PERFORMANCE CLIPS STILL OWE AN EAR CHECK (MPI-622's open item). The 12 R1/R3 ones he accepted. Relevant because a bad clip in those grids would present exactly as 'VC is inconsistent'.

A PEER SESSION'S MPI-629 ('Update button in Settings') sits in `tasks/` but is NOT in board.json, so `validate_board.py` FAILS on an orphaned task folder. Not mine, created 09:25 by another session, deliberately left alone. Board validated clean before it appeared.

THE BENCH IS HOLDING ~4GB from a `--warm` run: `keep_model_loaded` parks models in the pack's module-level `_MODEL_CACHE`, which `model_management` never sees, so `POST /free` returns 200 having released nothing. Clears on restart.

key_decisions: THE USER'S EAR OUTRANKS THE MEASUREMENT, AND IT WAS RIGHT EVERY TIME THIS SESSION. He caught that q3 had no accent (the card already said exaggeration 0.8, and I had baked 0.5 carried over from a different purpose); he reframed accent->language, which reversed a recommendation I had already written into validation.md; and he caught a dropdown label that lies. Measure to CHECK a listener, never to overrule one.

A NEGATIVE RESULT IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE QUESTION IT ANSWERED. 'Accent on English does not work' was true and properly measured, and it nearly deleted the multilingual model - which the product needs for a completely different reason (non-English text) that nobody had put in front of me. Ask what a model is FOR before recommending its removal.

DO NOT CARRY A CONSTANT ACROSS A MODEL BOUNDARY. exaggeration 0.5/1.2 and cfg 0.3 are BASE-model findings. Reusing 0.5 on the multilingual arm produced q3's missing accent; reusing 1.2/0.3 there appears to produce no emotion at all. Only `repetition_penalty` 1.5 has actually been measured on multilingual.

COSINE ALONE IS NOT AN IDENTITY GATE - third time on this card. Order B scored 0.827 while being 5.35 semitones sharp, because CAMPPlus x-vectors are pitch-invariant by construction. The gate is cosine AND median-f0 delta, and only the f0 half caught it.

'IT RAN' IS NOT 'IT ROUTED'. Four quadrants all produced audio, which proves nothing - a lost MpiAnySwitch selector silently pins every run to any_1 and still succeeds. Distinctness of the four outputs is the real check, and it is cheap.

ASK BEFORE QUEUEING ANYTHING ON THE BENCH. It is a single-queue shared resource and Fabio was mid-test when a 6-job sweep interrupted him. He then said explicitly: do not do any tests on the bench. Hand him a loadable workflow instead.
constraints: DO NOT RUN ANYTHING ON THE BENCH WITHOUT ASKING. Standing instruction from Fabio this session, after a sweep interrupted his own testing.

PER-TASK AND STATE EVENT LOGS TAKE DIFFERENT SHAPES: `tasks/<id>/events.jsonl` wants {schema,id,type,at,actor,summary}; `state/events.jsonl` wants {schema,type,task,at,note}. Using the state shape in the task file fails validate_board.py with 'event schema must be mpi-kanban/event/v1' plus 'task event missing id'.
